title: Cohomological bound for a derived functor on unbounded complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be an additive functor on the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which commutes with countable direct products, and let $N\ge0$ be an integer. Suppose $R^pF(\mathcal F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $p\ge N$, where $RF$ and $R^pF$ are the right derived functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. If $b$ is an integer and $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] has $H^i(E)=0$ for $i>b$, then $H^i(RF(E))=0$ for $i>b+N-1$.

proof.text: Use the canonical reconstruction after RF supplied by [lem-pc-qcoh-truncation-derived-limit]. Construct its inverse-system functor using Functor.ofOpSequence and apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-milnor-sequence] in degree i.

The bound on E means E is in D≤b for the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]; hence its truncation τ≥(b+1)E is zero. The right derived functor sends zero objects to zero objects (Functor.isZero_rightDerivedFunctor_obj). Starting at n=-b-1, use integer induction and [lem-pc-derived-functor-truncation-stabilization] to show H^i(RF(E_n))=0 for every integer n≥-b-1. Each successor index n+1 is ≥N-i since i≥b+N.

For degree i-1 the successor transition of the natural-number truncation tower is invertible once n≥max(0,N-i), by [lem-pc-derived-functor-truncation-stabilization]. Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-eventually-iso] to make the left endpoint of the Milnor sequence zero.

The degree-i tower is eventually zero by the integer induction. For any j choose n=max(j,max(0,-b-1)). The projection of the inverse limit to term n is zero; cone compatibility along n→j implies the projection to j is zero. Limit extensionality therefore makes the inverse limit zero. Both endpoint maps of the Milnor short exact complex are zero; ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_X₂ gives H^i(RF(E))=0.
